Rhodium-Catalyzed Pauson–Khand-Type Cyclization of 1,5-Allene-
Alkynes:A Chirality Transfer Strategy for Optically Active Bicyclic
Ketones
Yulin Han,[a] Yichuan Zhao,[b] and Shengming Ma*[a, b]
Abstract: An efficient chirality transfer in the [RhCl(CO)2]2-
catalyzed [2++2++1] cyclization of optically active axially chiral
1,3-disubstituted allenynes with CO to access optically active
bicyclopentenone compoundsh as been developed. The
distal C=Cb ondo f allenesr eactedw ith the alknye unit and
CO to afford [4.3.0]-bicyclic products with high ee values
under mild reaction conditions with an excellent selectivity.
Introduction
Cyclopentenones are present in many important naturalp rod-
ucts and bioactive compounds (Scheme 1).[1–3] For example,
helenalina nd its derivatives have anti-cancer and anti-inflam-
matorye ffects, showing potential medicala pplications in the
treatment of deregulated and unwanted T-cell-mediated
immune responses.[2] In addition, tecomanine has ap owerful
hypoglycemic activity.[3]
The cyclopentenones are also useful building blocks or key
intermediates in total synthesis due to the versatility of the
enone moiety.T he Pauson–Khand reactionb etween an alkyne
and an alkene is one of the most powerful methodst os ynthe-
size the cyclopentenone skeleton.[4] When the alkene is re-
placedw ith an allene,b oth C=Cb onds of the allene unit may
react with the alkyne moiety.T hus, the control of which
double bond of the allene moiety reacts in the allenic Pauson–
Khand reaction( APKR) of 1,5-allenynes I is still ac hallenge
(Scheme2 A, pathsa and b).[4c, 5] Notably,i nt he Co-,[6] Mo-,[7]
and Ir-catalyzed[8] APKR, cyclopentenone derivatives II were the
major products. Brummond and Mukaie ta l. reported the Rh-
catalyzed reaction of allenynes with CO to produce cyclopente-
none compounds III,i nw hich the distal C=Cb ond of allenes

exclusively reacts with the alknyeu nit and CO (Scheme 2A ,
path b).[7e–g, 9, 10] FormalA lder-ene products, cross-conjugated
trienes IV,w ere also formed under inert atmosphere as report-
ed by Brummond[11a] and Shibata.[11b] Mukai[11c] and Brum-
mond[7f] also found that the Alder-ene products were obtained
as competing productsu nder CO atmosphere through an oxi-
dative cyclometalation/b-H elimination/reductive elimination
sequence (Scheme 2A ,p ath c).
On the other hand, in principle, chiral cyclopentenone com-
pounds could be accessed by chirality transfer when the opti-
cally active axially chiral allenynes are used. To our knowledge,
there are only limited examples on the APKR of chiral alleny-
nes.[7h, 12, 13] In 2002, Brummond et al. demonstrated ap artial
transfer of chirality for 1,5-allenynesi nt he Zr-o rM o-mediated
APKR to afford 2-cyclopentenones with the stereogenic center
beta to the carbonyl group (Scheme 2B ,l eft). In 2013, the
same group reported the RhI-catalyzedA PKR of 1,6-allenynes,
which afforded 5,7-bicyclic cyclopentenones with the stereo-
genic center adjacent to the carbonyl group with al ow ee
value probably due to sensitive a-H (Scheme 2B ,r ight). So far,
such reactions of 1,5-allenynes with an acceptable level of chir-
ality transfer have not been developed. Thus, the main chal-
lenges for this transformation would be the efficiency of the
chirality transfer and the easyr acemization of the products
due to the sensitive a-H in the bicyclic ketonep roducts.
Herein, the Rh-catalyzed APKR of 1,3-disubstituted allenynes to
synthesize optically active bicyclopentenones with excellent
enantioselectivities under mild reactionc onditions is reported
(Scheme 2C ).
Results and Discussion
We started this study by using racemic 1,3-disubstituted alle-
nyne 1a as the model substrate. After treatment with
[RhCl(CO)2]2 at 80 8C, the cross-conjugated triene 3a was
formed in 76 %y ield as the major product (Table1 ,e ntry 1). In-
terestingly,t he desired product 2a ,a rising from the reaction
between the distal C=Cb ond of the allene with the alkyne
and CO, was formed in 20 %y ield. There was no improvement
in neither the yield of 2a nor the selectivity when the reaction
was conducted at 60 8C( entry 2). When cationicr hodiumc om-
plex [Rh(cod)2]OTf was used as the catalyst,t he selectivity of
APKR and the yield of 2a weren oticeably improved (entry 3).
Next, the effect of silver salts was investigated (entries 4–10).
The reactionw as partially inhibited and yield of 2a wasl ower
when AgOAc or Ag3PO4 were added (entries 8a nd 10). The se-
lectivity and the yield of 2a decreased when AgOTfw as used
(entry 6), albeit there was as light improvementw hen AgBF4 or
AgClO4 were used (entries 4a nd 7). The yield of 3a dropped
to less than 10 %w ith the addition of AgSbF6 or AgOCOCF3
(entries 5a nd 9). The selectivity of 2a over 3a was furtheri m-
provedw hen the reactionw as carriedo ut at 10 8Ci nt he pres-
ence of AgSbF6 (entry 11). 3a was not detected when the reac-
tion was performed at5 8C( entry 12). Thus, the reaction of 1a
using [RhCl(CO)2]2 (2 mol %) and AgSbF6 (5 mol %) in toluene at
5 8Cw as chosen as the standard conditions for furthers tudy.

Next, the scope of the reactionw as investigated. Av ariety
of substrates containing NTsa st he linker afforded the prod-
ucts with yields of about 90 %a nd an excellent chirality trans-

alkyne substituted with Ph, CH3, as well as other synthetically
useful groups such as CO2Et, TMS and Br.T he substrates con-
tainingm alonate as the linker could also afford the desired
products with excellent chiralityt ransfer when the reaction
was carried out at room temperature (entries 6–8). Although
the reactiono f( Ra)-1h afforded 8% yield of cross-conjugated
triene 3h ,t he efficiency of chirality transfer for the formation
of 2h is still excellent( entry 8, Table 3). Finally,t he oxygen
atom could also be used as the linker for this reaction, afford-
ing the corresponding products (R)-2i –2j with high ee values
(entries9 –10).

Conclusions
A[ RhCl(CO)2]2/AgSbF6 co-catalyzed APKR of optically active ax-
ially chiral 1,3-disubstituted allenynes to preparec hiral cyclo-
pentenone compounds with an excellent efficiency of chirality
transfer has been developed. Alkyl, aryl as well as other
commonf unctional groups, such as silyl, ester and halogens,
are tolerated.T he mild reaction conditions, broad scope, and
excellent selectivity make this reaction an efficient method to
build the chiral cyclopentenone skeleton.
